name: guardrails
context: Any agent exposed to untrusted input or producing user-facing output: validation layers check prompts, completions, and tool payloads against safety policies such as PII, injection, toxicity, and scope.
benefits: PII redaction before logging or storage
avoid_when: Heavy check chains double latency on hot paths
The input is fully trusted and latency is the dominant constraint
anti_patterns: Policy only in the system prompt
design_principles: Decide fail-open versus fail-closed explicitly per policy
Validate every boundary crossing (input, tool result, output)
best_practices: Combine with step-budget for defense in depth
Enforce structured output schemas (JSON/YAML) to prevent injection via generated content
Run tool executions in sandboxed environments with minimal privileges
Apply least-privilege permissions scoped to current task
references: Beurer-Kellner et al., Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections, 2025 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08837
